about: Claims on the landing page that depend on work not yet merged to the public repository. Elements carrying data-gate="<id>" in index.html (and in tools/og-image.html, whose text ships inside assets/og-image.png) make the claim. A gate's optional "phrases" are case-insensitive words that only gated copy may use: `node site/tools/check.mjs` fails when one appears outside an element carrying that gate, so new copy cannot make a gated claim without a marker. `node site/tools/check.mjs --launch` (and `--stage`, which every deploy recipe in site/README.md uses) fails until every gate has a confirmed record and every outbound link plus every gate URL answers 2xx. To confirm a gate, check the claim against the public main branch or release named in `ref`, then replace null with {"by": "<name>", "on": "YYYY-MM-DD", "ref": "<commit or tag>", "note": "<what you checked>"}. If the claim is no longer true, change the copy instead and update the gate.

gates.claim: A one-command installer: `curl -fsSL https://github.com/stdevMac/payverge/releases/latest/download/install.sh | bash` on a Linux server with Docker asks for the domain and an admin email, generates the secrets, starts PostgreSQL, the API, the web app and Caddy from public container images, issues HTTPS certificates automatically and creates the admin account. Made by the hero 'Deploy in one command' button, the facts strip '1 command to deploy', How it works step 1 and the #deploy section (heading, lead, checklist, terminal).
gates.needs: deploy/install.sh, deploy/docker-compose.yml, deploy/Caddyfile and .github/workflows/release.yml at v1.0.0. The release workflow builds multi-arch GHCR images (SBOM, provenance, cosign) and attaches install.sh, so releases/latest/download/install.sh resolves (docs/governance/RELEASING.md).
gates.verify: Run the plan's headline acceptance test on a fresh VM with the exact command shown on the page. Confirm the prompts match the page copy and that the release asset is the reviewed deploy/install.sh of that tag.

confirmed.note: Fresh docker:dind host, the exact curl | bash command from the page. Prompts match the copy (domain or localhost, admin email, optional demo data). The served install.sh has the same sha256 as deploy/install.sh at v1.0.0 and as SHA256SUMS. Images pull anonymously, .env secrets are generated, every service turns healthy, /api/v1/health/ready answers 200 through Caddy and the admin signs in. Caddy issued its internal certificate for localhost; automatic HTTPS is configured, but a real Let's Encrypt issuance on a public domain was not exercised.

gates.claim: No third-party accounts are needed to start: files stay on a local volume and email goes to the logs until S3 or a mail provider is connected. Made by the hero note ('No sign-up, no account'), the facts strip '0 third-party accounts required' and the #deploy checklist.
gates.needs: The defaults at v1.0.0: STORAGE_DRIVER defaults to local (the backend_storage volume in deploy/docker-compose.yml), EMAIL_PROVIDER resolves to log when no key is set, and production preflight passes with only PUBLIC_URL, DB_PASSWORD, JWT_SECRET_KEY, PLUGIN_SECRET_KEY and the admin credentials (backend/internal/config/oss_preflight_matrix_test.go).
gates.verify: On the acceptance-test install with no optional env vars set: upload a menu photo and restart (the file survives on the volume); trigger an invite or password-reset email and find it in the backend logs; confirm no Stripe, Resend, S3 or other external credential is asked for.

confirmed.note: Same install, no optional env vars: no Stripe, Resend, S3 or other credential is asked for. An uploaded logo survives docker compose down/up with the same sha256. Password-reset and staff-invite emails appear in the backend log as "email not sent (EMAIL_PROVIDER=log)"; the body and links are logged only with EMAIL_LOG_CONTENT=true.

gates.claim: AI spend is tracked in a ledger. Daily dollar caps per venue and for the whole server are on by default whenever a model is configured, the amounts are configurable, and the guest waiter has a daily message limit. AI answers from your data and is off until a model is connected: an OpenRouter key, or an LLM_BASE_URL such as a self-hosted Ollama or vLLM server. Made by the AI band lead, the 'Spend you control' and 'Off until you turn it on' cards.
gates.needs: backend/cmd/app/oss_sec_ai.go at v1.0.0 enforces per-business ($5), instance-wide ($20) and guest-pool daily caps in every mode whenever a provider is configured (an unset or invalid value falls back to the default, never to no cap), AI_WAITER_DAILY_MESSAGE_BUDGET caps guest waiter messages, and LLM_BASE_URL selects any OpenAI-compatible endpoint (docs/self-hosting/ai.md).
gates.verify: On the public main branch, check that backend/cmd/app/oss_sec_ai.go (or its replacement) still enforces the per-business and instance-wide daily caps in every mode, that AI_WAITER_DAILY_MESSAGE_BUDGET still applies, and that with no OPENROUTER_API_KEY, LLM_API_KEY or LLM_BASE_URL set GET /api/v1/instance reports features.ai=false. Reword the 'Spend you control' and 'Off until you turn it on' cards if the knobs changed.

confirmed.note: backend/cmd/app/oss_sec_ai.go caps every mode once a provider is configured: $5 per business, instance-wide max($20, 2x business), guest pool half of the instance cap; invalid values fall back to the defaults. AI_WAITER_DAILY_MESSAGE_BUDGET (default 2000) still applies. With no key or LLM_BASE_URL, /api/v1/instance reports features.ai=false. On a local LLM_BASE_URL without OPENROUTER_PRICES, unpriced models book $0, so only the message budget bounds them.

gates.claim: The hero lead (QR ordering, a kitchen display, bills and payments, reservations and delivery, on your own server, with no platform fees), the facts strip (21 guest languages, 4 online payment rails plus cash), the eight feature cards, the 'Configure with the AI' step, the optional integrations list (payment providers, a model via an OpenRouter key or a self-hosted Ollama or vLLM server, Telegram alerts), the meta/OpenGraph/Twitter descriptions and the subtitle baked into assets/og-image.png describe the public tree.

Four payment rails plus cash, KDS, 58/80 mm printers, equal/custom/by-item splits, Z report, reservation approval, delivery tracking, Ops/Director, ARCA (beta) and AGENTS.md are on main.

gates.claim: A public demo at https://demo.payverge.io/ where anyone can enter a seeded restaurant as owner, staff or guest without signing up, and which resets every night at 03:00 UTC. It runs with no AI model connected and online payments (cards and USDC) off; guests pay at the counter. Made by the hero and closing 'Try the live demo' buttons, the nav 'Live demo' button, the closing heading and the 'Can I try it before installing?' answer.
gates.needs: The demo bundle (deploy/demo/, docs/self-hosting/public-demo.md) and DEMO_MODE at v1.0.1 (which contains the staff sign-in fix), deployed to the demo host with a pristine snapshot taken on v1.0.1 and the nightly reset timer enabled.
gates.verify: Open https://demo.payverge.io/, enter as Owner, as Staff (kitchen) and as a guest from the banner's table links; confirm the banner shows the 03:00 UTC reset, that the AI waiter answers as a menu helper (no model connected) and checkout offers only paying at the counter, and that `systemctl list-timers payverge-demo-reset.timer` on the demo host shows the next run. The URL probe checks that the demo answers.

confirmed.note: demo.payverge.io serves build 3740c43@1.0.1 (backend and frontend 1.0.1 from GHCR); the pristine snapshot was re-taken on 1.0.1 after a --maintenance reset. In headless Chromium, Owner lands on the dashboard and Staff (kitchen) and Staff (waiter) land on the Bodegón Mesa Larga venue dashboard, not the spinner. The banner shows the 03:00 UTC reset. A guest from a banner table link ordered a bundle (Order Submitted!) and the bill offers only paying with the cashier. Parrilla Quebracho Azul tables open the 'Mozo, menu helper' that says it is not an AI; /api/v1/instance reports ai, crypto and fiscal_ar false. The 2026-10-11 03:00 UTC timer run reset ok in 48s and the hourly watchdog check passed; the next run is listed by systemctl list-timers.
